title: A randomised trial of the bone formation after maxillary sinus floor augmentation with bovine hydroxyapatite (Cerabone®) and Photobiomodulation: histomorphometric and immunohistochemical analysis
authors: Klassmann, F. A., Ervolino, E., Kluppel, L. E., Theodoro, L. H., Mulinari-Santos, G., & Garcia, V. G. (2023). Journal of clinical and experimental dentistry, 15(7), e542–e550.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Low-power laser-mediated by PBM promoted greater bone formation; the newly formed tissue showed a more advanced state of bone maturation in maxillary sinuses filled with Cerabone® biomaterial and treatment with PBM, within the 30-day evaluation period. Key words: Sinus floor augmentation, dental implants, bone and bones, low-level light therapy” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
